corrections.claimed_speedup: Old README at commit 0db1ba2 (tables inherited from bc7enc16, same rows as the richgel999/bc7enc README), 31 images (kodim plus others), encode time only, multithreaded. Perceptual (average REC709 luma PSNR): ispc_texcomp slow 355.4 s at 48.6 dB vs bc7enc16 uber4/max_partitions 64 122.6 s at 50.0 dB (2.9x, derived from page data) and vs uber0/max_partitions 64 38.3 s at 49.6 dB (9.3x, derived from page data); ispc_texcomp basic 100.2 s at 48.3 dB vs uber0/max_partitions 16 20.8 s at 49.3 dB (4.8x, derived from page data); ispc_texcomp fast 41.5 s at 48.0 dB vs the same 20.8 s at 49.3 dB (2.0x, derived from page data); ispc_texcomp ultrafast 1.9 s at 46.2 dB vs uber0/max_partitions 0 8.9 s at 48.4 dB (bc7enc16 4.7x slower, derived from page data). Non-perceptual (average RGB PSNR): ispc_texcomp slow 355.4 s at 46.8 dB vs uber4/max_partitions 64 51 s at 46.1 dB (7.0x, derived) and vs uber0/max_partitions 64 29.3 s at 45.8 dB (12.1x, derived, 1.0 dB lower); ispc_texcomp basic 99.9 s at 46.5 dB vs 51 s at 46.1 dB (2.0x, derived, 0.4 dB lower); ispc_texcomp fast 41.5 s at 46.1 dB vs uber1/max_partitions 16 19.8 s at 45.5 dB (2.1x, derived, 0.6 dB lower) and vs uber0/max_partitions 8 10.46 s at 44.4 dB (4.0x, derived, 1.7 dB lower); ispc_texcomp ultrafast 1.9 s vs 3.8 s at 42.7 dB (bc7enc16 2x slower). Update row (latest bc7enc16, uber4/max_partitions 64): ispc_texcomp fast 41.45 s at 46.09 dB RGB vs bc7enc16 41.42 s at 46.03 dB (parity; 38.78 s at 45.94 dB with filterbank optimizations). DirectXTex CPU mode-6-only 466.4 s at 41.9 dB vs bc7enc16 mode 6 only 6.7 s at 42.8 dB (about 70x, derived); DirectXTex default (no 3-subset modes) 9485.1 s at 45.6 dB vs uber1/max_partitions 64 36 s at 46.0 dB (about 263x, derived). The current README has no benchmark tables.
corrections.license: MIT OR Unlicense for the repo's own sources (bc7enc, rgbcx, ert); bc7e.ispc is Apache-2.0 (Binomial LLC); LodePNG carries its own license (see lodepng.cpp)
corrections.caveats: Duplicate of richgel999/bc7enc (verified, tier C): the README tables at commit 0db1ba2 are byte-identical to the bc7enc README tables and describe the bc7enc16 encoder (modes 1 and 6, scalar), and the README itself says it 'still refers to bc7enc16, but bc7enc is the same encoder but with more alpha modes'. The other BC7 encoder in this repo is bc7e.ispc, already listed as BinomialLLC/bc7e; this repo holds its latest version (determinism fix, better solid-colour blocks). What bc7enc_rdo adds is RDO post-processing (ert) and reduced-entropy BC7 for smaller LZ-compressed size, which is a size feature with no speed claim. The README says most timings are for the original bc7enc16 release and that later versions are 8-27% faster at the same quality. Hardware is 'a dual Xeon workstation' (no model), OpenMP thread count, compiler and flags are not given (the old README's 'tested MSVC 2019 x64 and clang 6.0.0' refers to building this repo, not to the 2018 benchmark), and no comparison harness is in the repo. Perceptual rows are scored on luma PSNR, which bc7enc16's perceptual mode optimizes and ispc_texcomp does not; at matched RGB PSNR the update row shows parity with ispc_texcomp fast, and ispc_texcomp ultrafast is faster. The DirectXTex run used a locally patched pbit-bugfix build, and DirectXTex's CPU BC7 path is a very slow baseline, so 70x and 263x overstate the practical gain. Last code commit was 2021-03-06 (merge of PR #4, bc7e improvements); every later commit through 2026-07-31 edits README.md or LICENSE (the 2026 notes point to the faster bc7f and to the plain C++ port of bc7e in basis_universal). Status is 'active' only by the last-commit rule. MIT/Unlicense option has no patent grant.

notes: Recommend decision duplicate folding into https://github.com/richgel999/bc7enc (same benchmarked encoder, same tables; that entry already names bc7enc_rdo as its maintained successor), with the bc7e.ispc part covered by https://github.com/binomialllc/bc7e. If the orchestrator keeps it as its own entry, it is a tier C confirm with the corrected claim and caveats. Metadata checked on github.com: 282 stars, 62 forks, not archived, not a fork; richgel999/bc7enc16 README returns 404 on raw.githubusercontent.com.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the criterion harness that produced PR #50's 256x256 table is public at benches/compress.rs on the tests-and-benches and arm64-perf branches (open PR #48; bench_presets, synthetic 256x256 'natural' image, 1 thread), the ISPC flags are in build.rs (opt_level 2, neon-i32x8, CPU pinned to apple-a14, prebuilt kernels checked in), the compiler is stated (ISPC 1.31 on LLVM 23, ISPC 1.20 for the main column) and the CPU is an Apple M5 Max. The baseline is Intel's unmodified upstream ISPCTextureCompressor kernels run through the same binding and harness, and the PR #49 column holds the compiler fixed, so this is a fork-against-upstream comparison with output quality matched (BC7 PSNR within 0.0001 dB), not a self-comparison of the project's own earlier code; the 4K table and the bc7e comparison have no public runner and are C-level.

Full 4096x4096 example texture, single thread, best of 2 runs: all presets 255.64 s to 108.69 s (2.35x), bc7_opaque/basic 13.39 s to 5.25 s (2.55x), etc1 16.32 s to 2.86 s (5.71x). Follow-up PR #51 (merged into arm64-perf): bc7e-style partition ranking, opaque presets 0.95-1.73x on 24 Kodak images and 1.00-1.75x on the 4K texture vs the post-#50 state, with presets retuned at equal or higher PSNR; its text says bc7e is slower on the 4K texture on the same machine (veryfast 2.38 s vs 1.05 s at 51.27 dB, 2.3x; basic 8.84 s vs 5.21 s, 1.7x; derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: ISPC 1.31 (LLVM 23) for the PR #49 and PR #50 columns, ISPC 1.20 for main. build.rs (ispc feature): ISPC opt_level(2); aarch64 target neon-i32x8 with CPU pinned to apple-a14 on macOS (x86 targets SSE2, SSE4, AVX1, AVX2, AVX512SKX-x16); the kernel libraries are prebuilt and checked into src/ispc, which is what the bench links. Rust release profile lto = true, opt-level = 3, codegen-units = 1 (Cargo.toml). Harness benches/compress.rs with criterion 0.8 (tests-and-benches and arm64-perf branches, open PR #48). rustc version not stated.
corrections.workload: Single-threaded block encode of a 256x256 procedural 'natural' test image (tests/common/mod.rs, seeded RNG) for every BC6H and BC7 preset (criterion, sample size 10), plus BC1-BC5 and ETC1 slow at 64, 256 and 1024 px; separately a full 4096x4096 photo (examples/lambertian.jpg) across all presets, best of 2 runs, with no runner in the repository.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 17 stars, 3 forks; crates.io intel_tex_2 0.5.0 (2025-07-02), 680,756 downloads total, 169,928 recent (crates.io API, 2026-10-04)
corrections.caveats: Unreleased and not on main: PRs #49, #50 and #51 were merged into a stack of branches (#49 into tests-and-benches, #50 into ispc-1.31, #51 into arm64-perf) that waits on open PR #48 into main; main's last commit is 2026-07-01 and crates.io 0.5.0 (2025-07-02) has the old kernels. The kernel changes live in the fork Traverse-Research/ISPCTextureCompressor (ISPC, C-callable; MIT, Intel copyright), which is the code a C++ user would take; this crate is its Rust binding. Only Apple Silicon was measured; the PR says x86, Windows, Linux and Android binaries were regenerated but not benchmarked, and much of the gain comes from removing per-lane gathers that NEON lacks, which 'matters less on AVX2/AVX-512', so the x86 gain over Intel's kernels is unknown and could be small. The 256x256 presets run on one synthetic image; the 4K numbers (best of 2) and the bc7e comparison in PR #51 have no runner in the repo, and bc7e's ISPC build for NEON is not described. ETC1 output is not bit-identical (last 4 commits change tie-breaking, +0.0010 dB measured against PR #49 because main's ETC1 aborts on an uninitialized-memory bug); BC6H moved -0.0004 to +0.0027 dB, mostly from the ISPC version change. PR #51 retunes the BC7 presets while keeping their names, so post-#51 presets do different work than upstream presets of the same name (PSNR equal or higher). PR text was read through a page summarizer on several fetches that agreed on every quoted row and whose ratios recompute from the times; treat per-row values as quoted. Dual MIT or Apache-2.0; vendored kernels MIT.

notes: The orchestrator's 'no Criterion harness found' does not hold: benches/compress.rs exists on the non-default branches tests-and-benches and arm64-perf (open PR #48 into main), so I upgraded to A for the 256x256 Apple M5 Max table; if the orchestrator treats an unmerged branch harness or the missing rustc version as disqualifying, C is the fallback. Cross-reference for bc7e (listed, B): on ARM the improved Intel kernels beat bc7e per PR #51 (first-party, no harness). Language stays Rust for the binding, but the kernels are ISPC in Traverse-Research/ISPCTextureCompressor.

tier_reason: The README gives absolute GPU encode and decode timings (gpujpegtool -n 100, 99-run averages) but no comparison against libjpeg-turbo, nvJPEG or any other codec, and FAQ.md and NEWS.md compare only against GPUJPEG's own earlier versions. The only cross-codec numbers are a user's 2020 nvJPEG comparison (issues #47 and #48, the same post twice), which is mixed and has no GPU, CUDA version or method, so there is no supported faster-than-baseline number: D.

corrections.caveats: No numeric comparison against libjpeg-turbo, nvJPEG or any CPU codec in the README, FAQ.md or NEWS.md (NEWS only cites self-comparisons such as first-frame start-up 43 ms vs 810 ms, about 20x, and an IDCT kernel 43% faster). The only cross-codec numbers are one user's September 2020 post, filed twice as issues #47 and #48 with identical text and no maintainer reply visible: on an 8192x8192 random texture total time was 911.242 ms for GPUJPEG vs 1608.21 ms for nvJPEG (1.8x, derived), but on a portrait with a uniform background 620.884 ms vs 441.444 ms (nvJPEG 1.4x faster, derived); GPU, CUDA version and method are not given, times include I/O, and GPUJPEG's stream had 16384 restart segments against 1 for nvJPEG. Per the README, Huffman coding runs on the GPU only when restart markers are present; with restart interval 0 the CPU Huffman coder is used, so JPEGs from other encoders without restart markers do not get the GPU Huffman path. README timings: a hidden comment says the RTX 4080 rows came from a cmake build without Release or CUDA-architecture flags with 5 measurements averaged (the visible text says 99 measurements), and another hidden note says other measurements were done without CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release. Host CPU, CUDA toolkit and driver versions are not stated. The peer-reviewed description (Holub et al., 'GPU-accelerated DXT and JPEG compression schemes for low-latency network transmissions of HD, 2K, and 4K video', Future Generation Computer Systems, 2013) could not be opened here (ScienceDirect, ACM and ics.muni.cz blocked), so any CPU comparison in it is unverified. A check against a CPU baseline is needed before listing it as faster than libjpeg-turbo.

notes: All README timings quoted in the record match the page (4K encode 1.65 ms RTX 4080, 1.71 ms RTX 3080, 2.89 ms RTX 2080 Ti, 3.16 ms RX 7600 via ZLUDA; 8K 6.33 ms; 16K 24.92 ms; decode 4K 1.46 ms, 8K 5.78 ms; RTX 3080 8K q70 6.21 ms, 2.28 ms without PCIe).
